chunks: My father narrated to me, from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Ya’qūb ibn Yazīd, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali, from Yūnus ibn Rafī’, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:
There is indeed at the head of al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Ali (peace be upon him) a red dust, in which is a cure for every disease except death (al-sām).

He said: So I went to the grave after we had heard this ḥadīth, and we dug at the head of the grave. When we had dug about an ell, red dust like sand, about the size of a dirham, flowed down upon us from the head of the grave. We carried it to Kūfah, mixed it, and stored it. Then we began giving it to the people, and they would cure themselves with it.

key_terms.السَّام: Death (specifically fatal disease or death itself)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and physical significance of the red dust from the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the Shia belief in the physical presence of healing properties (barakah) in the earth of Imam al-Ḥusayn’s grave, specifically noting the exception of 'al-sām' (death or incurable plague). The account underscores the practical application of this tradition, where the collected red dust was mixed and distributed in Kufa as a tangible remedy, reflecting the interplay between spiritual reverence and physical healing in Shia piety.
